external.title: Efference Copy Is Necessary for the Attenuation of Self-Generated Touch
external.read_scope: Primary indexed abstract and figure captions via web search; direct open returned a footer/PMC recaptcha. No raw-data reanalysis.
external.finding_scope: In this self-touch design active but not passive triggering attenuated perceived intensity. This supports source-sensitive mechanisms in a particular protocol, not a universal gate or H identity.

external.title: Movement enhances tactile sensitivity through prediction
external.read_scope: Publisher search retrieval: abstract, introductory distinctions, publication history and data link. Data not downloaded/reanalysed.
external.finding_scope: Matched active/passive kinematics separate reduced felt intensity from enhanced sensitivity. Distinct readouts must not be collapsed into one attenuation or agency scalar.

external.title: Sensory Attenuation Reflects Proprioceptive Recalibration Rather Than Motor Forward Models
external.read_scope: Primary preprint abstract via search; direct open 403, full methods/raw data not read.
external.finding_scope: The abstract reports passive transport with comparable attenuation and proprioceptive predictability dependence. Treat as provisional challenge to universal motor-copy necessity, not a replicated refutation of every earlier protocol.

synthesis: Frontier evidence constrains candidate mechanisms and readout specificity. It does not validate C1 or assign familiar self-related feeling to model coordinates. Different protocols and preprint status prevent declaring the 2020 result globally refuted.
